_what: Hashes of the frozen rules. A change here without an amendment is the gate's SAFETY block.
_rule: If a rule is wrong, the human changes it and the tests follow — never the reverse.

amendments.what: First run showed the draft targeted /contacts, a super-admin-only route that redirects members before any tenant filter runs, and asserted an HTTP 404 that a streamed route cannot return. Retargeted at the workspace-scoped contacts list and asserted on disclosure instead of status, so the test fails on a real leak rather than on its own mechanics.

Second correction after running: the client contacts tab renders contact LISTS not addresses, so it could not carry the spec's recipient rows. Retargeted at the workspace overview (identity) and the activity feed (real prospect addresses and subjects), and added an explicit positive control.

BC-01 retargeted from /contacts (super-admin only, redirects members before any tenant filter) to surfaces that actually render tenant data, after the original test scored a false green on the wrong route
BC-01 asserted staff-level isolation the product deliberately does not have; retargeted to workspace DATA isolation, with the access decision and its reversal trigger recorded

Rewritten alongside the BC-01 spec: the old tests asserted staff-level access isolation the product deliberately does not have. Retargeted at workspace DATA isolation (R-1, R-5, R-6) plus the authentication wall (E-03), with a positive control and an explicit note that these did not go red first

Positive control asserts DOM presence, not visibility: the activity feed sits in a collapsed <details>, and data delivered to another workspace's browser is disclosed whether or not CSS is painting it
